messages:
incident-bot: [SEV-2] Elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate across multiple edge regions. auto-group=cloudflare-edge-tls. Paging network-oncall. :rotating_light:
Mira Chen: seeing a big jump in TLS failures from several PoPs. dashboards show 525/526 spikes, few 524 timeouts too.
Samir Patel: reproducing locally from eu-north probe: TLS alert during handshake. curl output:
Samir Patel: ```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
*   Trying 198.51.100.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (198.51.100.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error: TLS handshake failed
```
Priya Gupta: monitoring note: datadog ingest has a 6m gap around the same window (1933334300-1933334660). traces are patchy. raised ticket with datadog but not high priority from them.
Alex Rogers: quick check of origin: direct-curl to origin ip responds fine, cert chain valid. so origin seems healthy. pointing to CF edge being the problem.
Jordan Lee: running distributed probes now (us-west, eu-north, ap-southeast). initial numbers: us-west 68% handshake fail, eu-north 60%, ap-southeast 12%.
Samir Patel: edge LB logs show SNI mismatch / unexpected client_hello modifications from a subset of CF PoPs. message: "received SNI different from expected; rejecting". opening Cloudflare enterprise slack and creating ticket.
Mira Chen: Samir take lead on CF ticket. I'll coordinate customer comms and support response.
pagerduty-bot: Paging Samir Patel (oncall-network)  acknowledged by Samir Patel.
Samir Patel: CF case created (ref 87654321). reached engineer; they suspect a config push that rewrote SNI in some POPs. they're investigating rollback.
Priya Gupta: mitigation suggestion: begin origin log tail + quick analysis to estimate request impact. if CF rollback >20m, plan DNS bypass. I'm starting the log harvest to S3 now.
Alex Rogers: proposed operational mitigation: create short-lived A records api-bypass.redwood-inference.com -> origin public IPs, TTL=15s, then shift weighting in Route53 to send 25% traffic to bypass for affected regions. can do per-region using geoproximity policies.
Jordan Lee: caveat: if we split traffic we might see mixed path behavior for clients with long-lived connections. prefer full cutover for short window if rollback ETA exceeds 30min.
Samir Patel: CF replied: "we're rolling back the problematic edge config; rollback propagation started. estimated impact reduction in 10-25m." they provided status link: https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/edge-config-1933
Mira Chen: hold on DNS flip for now. avoid split-path until we confirm. notify support to use canned reply: "We're investigating TLS handshake failures for some regions routed via Cloudflare. Engineering is working with Cloudflare on a rollback. We'll update in 15 minutes."
network-bot: telemetry: end-to-end handshake success dropped from 99.98% to 57% at peak across affected PoPs.
Priya Gupta: datadog gap partially recovered; using origin access logs we've estimated ~11-16% of requests in the 18m window returned 5xx. building a customer impact matrix by account tier.
Samir Patel: CF update: rollback completed for 70% of PoPs; working through remaining PoPs. their internal signals show TLS failures decreasing.
Jordan Lee: continued probes show improvement: us-west failure rate down to 12%, eu-north down to 9% now.
Alex Rogers: prepping post-rollback verification steps: 1) run 10m synthetic with 1s p95 < 200ms and 5xx < 0.5% 2) validate logs are flowing into observability 3) clear status when stable.
Mira Chen: notifying customers with SLA contracts via the incident contact list. short note: we had transient TLS handshake issues via Cloudflare affecting API reachability in some regions; mitigation in progress. will update on resolution.
Samir Patel: Cloudflare confirmed full rollback. final probe shows TLS handshake success >99.7% across PoPs. No origin changes required.
Priya Gupta: uploaded harvested origin logs and a CSV of impacted request IDs to the incident bucket. rough customer impact: ~14% of requests across the 20m window experienced 5xx; highest hit on US-West and EU-North.
Mira Chen: marking incident as mitigated. leaving channel open for 45m for monitoring. creating postmortem ticket and assigning action items: add multi-pop TLS health checks, automated failover to backup CDN provider, and runbook for DNS bypass.
Samir Patel: FYI I've asked CF for RCA and details on the config change that triggered the regression; will attach to postmortem when available.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff: Samir -> Mira in 10m.
incident-bot: Incident SEV-2  mitigated (third-party). Follow-up: postmortem ticket /docs/incidents/1933334444-postmortem (owner: Mira Chen).
Mira Chen: thanks everyone for quick coordination. please add any notes to the postmortem doc.
Alex Rogers: adding a note to track DNS low-TTL readiness and dry-run the bypass next week.
Jordan Lee: will add probe coverage for additional CF PoPs to catch regressions earlier.
Mira Chen: closing channel in 45m unless we see a regression. :white_check_mark:
